identity.title: Nuclear kinematics in nearby AGN - I. An ALMA perspective on the morphology and kinematics of the molecular CO(2-1) emission
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present the molecular gas morphology and kinematics of seven nearby Seyfert galaxies obtained from our 230 GHz ALMA observations.

question.value: What are the morphology and kinematics of CO(2-1) in the inner kpc of seven nearby Seyfert galaxies, and how do they deviate from circular rotation?

evidence.quote: The CO J=2-1 kinematics within the inner $\sim30\ensuremath{''}$ ($\lesssim9$ kpc) reveals rotation patterns that have been explored using the Bertola rotation model and a modified version of the *Kinemetry* package.
All galaxies were observed with ALMA during Cycles 2 (project-ID 2012.1.00474.S; PI - Nagar) and 4 (project-ID 2015.1.00086.S; PI - Nagar).

The observations were taken using the ALMA Band 6 receivers on thirty-two 12-meter antennas.
The SPWs were thus centred on 229.415 GHz, 227.060 GHz, 241.554 GHz and 243.735 GHz, with bandwidths of 1.875 GHz, 2.0 GHz, 1.875 GHz and 1.875 GHz, respectively
$^{b}$ Noise per 2.6 km s$^{-1}$ channel.

analysis_steps.goal: Calibrate, self-calibrate and image CO(2-1) cubes

method.value: CASA calibration, uv continuum subtraction, self-cal applied, natural-weighted imaging at 2.6 km/s

evidence.quote: Data were calibrated and imaged using CASA 4.7.0 (cite: McMullin2007).

analysis_steps.goal: Make moment maps M0, M1, M2

method.value: Moments computed with 4 sigma threshold using all channels with CO emission

evidence.quote: we generated moment maps assuming a threshold of $4\sigma$ with the noise level shown in Table [\[obsPar\]](#obsPar).

key_parameters.value: channels with CO emission, typically 250 to 600

evidence.quote: All channels with visible CO emission (typically 250 to 600 channels) were used in the calculation of the moment maps.

assumptions.value: M2 treated as upper limit on intrinsic dispersion

evidence.quote: even though they show the upper limit of the intrinsic velocity dispersion especially in the nuclear regions

analysis_steps.goal: Fit Bertola rotation model to velocity maps

method.value: Fit eq. of Bertola 1991 to M1 map, five parameters free, p in 1.0-1.5, also fit centre; minimise rms of residuals

evidence.quote: allowing five of the six parameters of the model to vary freely, with the sixth ($p$) allowed to vary in the range $1.0 - 1.5$.

assumptions.value: circular orbits in a spherical potential

evidence.quote: we assume circular orbits in a spherical potential as given in (cite: Bertola1991).

fitting.value: MADS direct search, minimising rms of residuals

evidence.quote: The best-fitting parameters were obtained by minimising a root-mean-square value of the residuals
In all our simulations, the optimisation routine was able to recover the parameters to within an error of 1%.

analysis_steps.goal: Run modified Kinemetry (modKin) on M1 maps

method.value: Fourier decomposition in elliptical rings; 4 terms for PA, flattening and centre, then rerun at fixed values with ten Fourier terms; velocity map weighted 1/M1err^2

evidence.quote: Upon obtaining these values, we ran the *modKin* code again at these fixed values for ten Fourier terms.

key_parameters.value: COVER = 0.50; 100 ellipses initially; ring spacing set by beam size

evidence.quote: we provided the *COVER* parameter of 0.50 as input along with the boundary values for the centre coordinates.

fitting.value: MADS replaces grid plus Levenberg-Marquardt; bounds Gamma in [-90,90], q in [0,1]

evidence.quote: for the position angle ($\Gamma \in [-90, 90]$) and the flattening ($q \in [0, 1]$)
We tested the adopted optimisation algorithm with the Bertola model and *modKin* code on 1000 different simulated velocity maps with known sets of parameters.

method.value: Search best-fit centre within 5 arcsec of continuum peak; adopt modKin; new estimate only if offset from 2MASS exceeds beam major axis

evidence.quote: we consider the centre coordinates as a new estimate only if the difference in value is larger than the synthesized beam major axis.

validation.value: Bertola and modKin agree within a few pixels

evidence.quote: The result obtained from both the models seem to agree within a few ($\pm5$) pixels.

analysis_steps.goal: Classify kinematics and compute photometric-kinematic misalignment

method.value: Classification by SAURON/ATLAS3D scheme; misalignment via Franx 1991 sinPsi relation, misaligned if Psi>10 deg

evidence.quote: We classify all galaxies with $\Psi > 10^{\circ}$ as being misaligned.
Data were calibrated and imaged using CASA 4.7.0 (cite: McMullin2007).
We refer to our modified version of the Kinemetry as *modKin* in the following sections.

used_for.value: optimisation for Bertola and modKin fits

evidence.quote: We therefore use the MADS[^2] algorithm for all our analysis.

findings_qualitative.value: All seven galaxies show deviations from pure circular rotation in the inner kpc: twists, decoupled and counter-rotating cores

evidence.quote: reveals various deviations from pure circular rotation in the inner kiloparsec of all seven galaxies, including kinematic twists, decoupled and counter-rotating cores.

findings_qualitative.value: CO and stellar PA and Vsys agree, inclination differs more

evidence.quote: show overall agreement in the position angle of the major axis and the systemic velocity, but larger discrepancies in the disc inclination.

claims.hypothesis: Does the nuclear CO kinematics follow pure circular rotation?
claims.experiment: Bertola and modKin fits to CO M1 maps
claims.result: Residuals and local profiles show twists, a decoupled core in NGC 1386 and a counter-rotating core in NGC 1667
claims.finding: All galaxies are multi-component systems with non-circular motions

evidence.quote: we are able to identify all galaxies as multi-component systems.

claims.hypothesis: Do molecular gas and stellar global kinematics agree?
claims.experiment: Compare PA, inclination and Vsys from modKin and Bertola with literature stellar values
claims.result: PA within ~10 deg, Vsys within ~20 km/s, inclination up to ~16 deg discrepant
claims.finding: Agreement in PA and Vsys, discrepancy in inclination

evidence.quote: Inclination seems to be the one with a relatively larger discrepancy, reaching as high as $\sim16^{\circ}$.

claims.hypothesis: Are photometric and kinematic axes misaligned?
claims.result: ESO 428-G14, NGC 3081, NGC 5728, NGC 7213 have Psi>10 deg

evidence.quote: This makes ESO 428-G14, NGC 3081, NGC 5728 and NGC 7213 as misaligned candidates.

why_this_method.value: 2D modelling used because 3D packages lack features to constrain non-axisymmetric structure

evidence.quote: we only consider the 2D modelling approach owing to the lack of features in the mentioned 3D packages to constrain or demarcate the non-axisymmetric features effectively.
Some of the well-known packages are GalPaK (cite: Bouche2015), $^{3{D}}$BAROLO (cite: DiTeodoro2015) and TiRiFiC (cite: Jozsa2007).

limitations_admitted.value: Results rely on intensity-weighted mean velocity maps; non-axisymmetric features not discussed

evidence.quote: the results reported in this work are primarily based on the interpretation of the intensity weighted mean velocity maps.

limitations_admitted.value: NGC 7213 sparse data prevented modKin fits

evidence.quote: NGC 7213 (was impossible to obtain meaningful fits from owing to the sparse information)

referee_caveats_inferred: Moment-1 maps with 4 sigma clipping can bias velocities near the nucleus due to beam smearing
Stellar comparison values come from heterogeneous literature sources
Uncertainties quoted only as 'within 5%' without a rigorous error analysis
Interpretations (mergers, external gas origin) are speculative
